summary: Meropenem is a broad-spectrum carbapenem antibacterial given IV for complicated skin and skin structure infections, complicated intra-abdominal infections, and bacterial meningitis (pediatrics). It requires renal dose adjustment and carries a risk of seizures and serious hypersensitivity.
indications: Complicated skin and skin structure infections (adults and pediatrics >=3 months)

dosage.d: 500 mg IV every 8 hours (1 g q8h if Pseudomonas aeruginosa)
dosage.n: IV infusion over 15-30 min or bolus over 3-5 min
IV infusion over 15-30 min or bolus over 3-5 min

dosage.d: cSSSI 10 mg/kg q8h (max 500 mg); intra-abdominal 20 mg/kg q8h (max 1 g); meningitis 40 mg/kg q8h (max 2 g)

admin: Administer IV only - by infusion over 15-30 minutes or IV bolus (5-20 mL) over 3-5 minutes
Reconstitute and dilute per labeling; use promptly
Obtain cultures before starting; de-escalate per susceptibility
Assess for prior beta-lactam/carbapenem hypersensitivity before first dose
moa: Meropenem is a carbapenem beta-lactam that readily penetrates the cell wall of most gram-positive and gram-negative bacteria and binds penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs), inhibiting bacterial cell wall synthesis and causing cell lysis. It is stable to hydrolysis by most beta-lactamases including many ESBLs and AmpC enzymes.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to any component of the product
relative: History of seizure disorder or CNS lesions
monitor: Signs of seizure or CNS effects

preg: Insufficient human data to establish drug-associated risk. Animal studies (rats, monkeys) showed no fetal toxicity or malformations at 2.3-2.4 times the MRHD. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed.
lact: Meropenem is present in human milk in small amounts; considered likely compatible. Consider developmental/health benefits of breastfeeding alongside maternal clinical need.
renal: Dose adjustment required for CrCl <=50 mL/min: CrCl 26-50 give recommended dose every 12 h; CrCl 10-25 give half dose every 12 h; CrCl <10 give half dose every 24 h. Meropenem is removed by hemodialysis - dose after dialysis.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment needed for hepatic impairment; monitor liver function (transient transaminase elevations may occur) in patients with pre-existing liver disease.

major: Valproic acid / divalproex sodium (markedly reduces valproate levels - risk of breakthrough seizures; avoid combination)
moderate: Probenecid (inhibits renal excretion, increases meropenem levels - not recommended)
interactions.diagnostics: May cause a positive direct or indirect Coombs test.

monitoring: Renal function and adjust dose accordingly
counsel: Given as an IV medication in a healthcare setting
Report rash, itching, swelling, or difficulty breathing immediately
Report severe or persistent diarrhea (even weeks after therapy)
Tell your clinician if you take valproate or have a seizure disorder
Complete the full course of antibiotics
pk: End of 30-min infusion: ~23 mcg/mL (500 mg), ~49 mcg/mL (1 g)
Store dry powder at 20-25 C; reconstituted solution use promptly per labeling
pearls: Time above MIC drives efficacy - maintain the q8h interval
Avoid with valproic acid; meropenem sharply lowers valproate levels
Adjust dose for renal impairment; dose after hemodialysis
Lower seizure potential than imipenem but still requires CNS caution
missed: Administered on a fixed schedule in a healthcare setting; if a dose is delayed, give as soon as possible and resume the q8h schedule. Not a self-administered drug.
overdose: No specific antidote. Discontinue and provide symptomatic/supportive care; meropenem and its metabolite are removed by hemodialysis.
